measure: periplasmic buffer capacity at own limit   (BUFFERING)

verdict: BURDEN, on the non-circular test. At pH 3 and 4 the charge change carries a POSITIVE coefficient, so acid-tolerant genomes have LESS outward-surface charge to change - which is what the burden account predicts - while buffer capacity carries a positive coefficient too, which is the OPPOSITE of what buffering predicts. This partly answers correction 21's tension: UreI needs its carboxylates because it is a gate that must respond, and bulk housekeeping surfaces appear to do better with fewer, which is the reconciliation stated in docs/EXPERIMENTAL_EVIDENCE.md section 2.2 - now with a measurement behind it rather than only an argument.
